jobgether-jobgether:lever:275608b6-4ada-.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst
jobgether-jobgether:lever:275608b6-4ada-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst based in Australia. This remote opportunity is designed for professionals and aspiring analysts looking to build practical experience in cyber threat intelligence through realistic, simulation-based environments. You will work with incomplete threat information, indicators, contextual data, and organizational requirements to determine what matters and why. The role emphasizes analytical judgment, source evaluation, threat prioritization, and decision-focused intelligence. You will translate technical findings into clear assessments and recommendations for different stakeholders. The work spans threat actors, TTPs, indicators, intelligence gaps, and evolving assessments. All activities are conducted in controlled environments for legitimate defensive, educational, and professional-development purposes. Triage and evaluate threat information: Review multiple sources of simulated threat intelligence, determine relevance, assess reliability and credibility, and identify information requiring further investigation. Analyze threats and adversary behavior: Assess simulated threat actors, including their motivations, capabilities, targeting patterns, tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), and determine their potential relevance to an organization. Assess indicators in context: Evaluate indicators of compromise alongside supporting evidence rather than treating individual indicators as definitive proof of malicious activity. Identify intelligence gaps: Determine what critical information is missing and define the additional intelligence required to improve security decision-making. Develop intelligence requirements: Create or refine priority intelligence questions based on organizational assets, threat exposure, business priorities, and stakeholder needs. Prioritize threats: Compare competing threats according to relevance, likelihood, potential impact, available evidence, and organizational priorities. Apply structured analytical reasoning: Evaluate competing hypotheses, weigh evidence, document assumptions, and communicate why one assessment may be better supported than another. Produce actionable intelligence: Synthesize multiple information sources into assessments explaining what is happening, why it matters, and what defensive priorities should be considered. Communicate analytical confidence: Clearly articulate confidence levels, evidence quality, assumptions, and factors that limit certainty. Brief decision-makers: Translate technical threat intelligence into concise, business-relevant insights and recommendations for senior or non-technical stakeholders. Update assessments: Reassess previous conclusions when new intelligence becomes available and clearly explain how additional evidence changes—or does not change—the original assessment. Create professional intelligence outputs: Develop threat assessments, threat actor profiles, executive intelligence briefs, intelligence requirements documents, TTP assessments, indicator assessments, confidence statements, threat prioritization reports, and intelligence updates. Requirements: Cybersecurity and threat intelligence interest: Suitable for aspiring CTI analysts, cybersecurity students or graduates, SOC professionals seeking CTI exposure, career changers, intelligence or security professionals transitioning into cyber, self-taught practitioners, and professionals with relevant cybersecurity certifications. Analytical reasoning: Ability to examine incomplete or conflicting information, identify patterns, weigh evidence, develop hypotheses, and reach reasoned conclusions. Threat intelligence fundamentals: Understanding of threat intelligence concepts, threat actors, indicators of compromise, TTPs, threat assessments, intelligence requirements, and risk prioritization. triedgeinvestments-triedge-investments:a.description: Co-Head, Axiom Private Credit About Axiom Private Credit Axiom Private Credit is a new, healthcare lending platform established under TriEdge Investments as a standalone strategy. The platform provides senior and subordinated mezzanine, secured financing to transitional skilled nursing and senior-care assets, including skilled nursing, assisted living, memory care, and independent living facilities. Rather than operating as a conventional balance-sheet lender, Axiom serves as an active bridge lender offering creative solutions including participating in the upside through preferred returns or warrants. Built on Hypha, TriEdge’s proprietary AI platform, Axiom is positioned to deploy efficiently and to expand beyond skilled nursing into healthcare credit more broadly. About TriEdge Investments TriEdge is a family office focused on building enduring value across healthcare, financial services, cybersecurity, defense technology and beyond. Founded in 2024 by Simcha Hyman, who brings 15+ years of experience building and exiting companies in healthcare and finance, TriEdge takes a multi-strategy approach, investing across stages and verticals including private equity, venture capital, real estate, and company incubation. With offices in New York City, Miami, and Tel Aviv, TriEdge brings together a team of seasoned operators, technologists, and investors to partner with founders building the technology-enabled platforms of tomorrow. Equally important to the mission is impact investing and philanthropy with a focus on mental health, education, and combating poverty and antisemitism. To learn more about our work, visit: https://www.triedgeinvestments.com/ What We’re Really Looking For We are seeking an experienced and analytically rigorous individual to launch and lead Axiom Credit as its full-time operating principal, working alongside a part-time co-head who provides legal and deal-execution oversight. The successful candidate will develop and oversee underwriting, origination and credit review; manage the platform’s assets on Hypha; and support expansion into adjacent healthcare verticals over time. Key Responsibilities · Build and manage a team to own end-to-end underwriting for transitional skilled nursing and senior-care credits, structuring each transaction with appropriate use of preferred returns, warrants, and downside protection. · Lead origination across the platform’s channels, including direct borrower relationships, brokers, and opportunities sourced through banking relationships. · Actively manage the loan portfolio, monitoring credit performance and intervening early to protect returns. · Develop the platform’s technology (Hypha) across underwriting, credit policy, covenant monitoring, servicing, and compliance, translating transaction logic into structured workflows. · Manage the pace and concentration of deployment across a high volume of small-balance transactions (generally under $20 million). · Support the platform’s growth, including relationships with lenders and prospective institutional partners, as the strategy scales toward larger facilities and additional verticals.
